data.name: Iolanthe
data.gender_notes: Iolanthe is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Iolanthe is the name of a nymph who was transformed into a violet flower. In Christianity, it is the name of a saint, Iolanthe of the Isles, who was a hermit and a healer. The name Iolanthe carries the meaning “Goddess of the night” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Iolanthe usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the night and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes transformation, spiritual growth, and healing.
data.etymology: Iolanthe belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of the night.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Iolanthe total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_english.name: Iolanthe
in_english.long_meaning: Christian name, description: 'religious origin' - The name Iolanthe originates from the Greek word 'ioulos' meaning 'throne' and in sequentia 'Iolanthe' meaning 'throne of God'. In Christian tradition, the name Iolanthe is associated with the divine throne and the heavenly kingdom. It symbolizes spiritual elevation, nobility, and a deep connection with the divine. In modern times, the name Iolanthe is used in various Christian cultures to signify a child's spiritual journey and their aspiration to reach the heavenly throne.

data.cultural_impact: Iolanthe is a beautiful and unique name with Greek origins, evoking images of mystical nymphs and ancient mythology. However, in Christian contexts, it takes on a new meaning as the name of a saint known for her sanctity and devotion.
data.spiritual_significance: Iolanthe's spiritual significance lies in her transformation - from a beautiful nymph to a violet flower, and later to a revered saint. This name signifies the idea of transformation and growth, both in the natural world and in the spiritual realm. It also serves as a reminder of the divine potential within each of us to transcend our current state and become something greater. Additionally, as a healer, Iolanthe represents the power of faith and the capacity to offer comfort and healing to those who seek it.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Iolanthe, meaning "violet" in Greek, symbolically represents the depth and richness of spiritual growth. It is a name for those who embody the radiant beauty of purified emotions and the strength of unyielding faith.

historical_references.reference: Iolanthe is a character in the opera 'Iolanthe' by W.S. Gilbert and Arthur Sullivan, first performed in London in 1882.
